transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. 

Um, I came in today because my behavior has just been kind of... extreme lately. I went from barely even settling into my new apartment to suddenly taking on way too much. I started saying yes to mentoring sessions, taking on extra client prototypes for work, and I even decided to redesign my whole portfolio. It was just like I had to fix my entire life in one giant sprint, and I guess I realized it's getting a bit out of hand.
During this period of high energy, have you experienced any thoughts or perceptions that others might find strange, such as hearing voices or believing things that others told you weren't true?

No, I haven't experienced anything like that. I don't hear voices, and I haven't believed anything that wasn't true. 

I mean, I definitely thought I could take on way more work than I actually had time for, but I was still completely in touch with reality. It was really just the intense energy and the urge to get a million things done, not anything strange like what you're describing.
Have you ever experienced a period in your life where you felt consistently low, sad, or hopeless for at least two weeks?

Yes, I have. Actually, lately I've been waking up with this... heavy, gray feeling in my chest. It's hard to explain, but even when my apartment is completely quiet and nothing bad is actually happening, I just feel so low. Like, I feel like I could just break down and cry over something as small as a coffee mug left in the sink. So, yeah, I definitely get those periods.
During your periods of high energy, have you ever felt so energized or irritable that it caused significant problems at work or in your relationships, or required you to be hospitalized?

No, it never got to that point. I haven't been hospitalized or anything like that. I mean, I definitely took on too much work, but it didn't cause any huge blow-ups or get me fired. It was more just... me running myself ragged trying to keep up with everything I agreed to do. My friends and coworkers probably thought I was just being a workaholic for a few weeks.
